text:
Ana (PM): quick sync — we need final acceptance criteria for the new "Onboarding + routing" quickstart. customer asked for a deterministic example they can copy-paste.
Sam (Eng): got it. are we keeping this docs-as-spec or separate short quickstart + deep-dive PRD?
Ana (PM): intention is docs-as-spec for the quickstart, and link to PRD for rollout rules. quickstart should be runnable in <15m and show 3 routing cases.
Ravi (Docs): proposed checklist: 1) minimal config example 2) expected outputs for each routing case 3) failure-mode notes + recovery 4) one end-to-end command (curl or SDK). anything missing?
Jess (Design): include an annotated screenshot of console route UI (mock), and a tiny sequence diagram for request->cache->fallback. visuals help reduce support asks.
Luis (Customer): for our customers the edge case is model mismatch on fallback. ask: can quickstart show a visible delta in output quality and show how to configure fallback thresholds?
Sam (Eng): yes. I can add a small snippet that toggles fallback by `max_latency_ms` and `quality_threshold`. show logs:
```
INFO routing: chosen model=redwood-alpha fallback=false latency=32ms
WARN routing: fallback to redwood-beta reason=timeout latency=980ms
```
Ravi (Docs): nice. for acceptance criteria we should require asserted outputs in the doc so CI can run an examples test. e.g., for input "summarize X" we assert contains key phrase Y.
Ana (PM): agreed — acceptance criteria draft: * quickstart runs in <=15m on hosted sandbox * shows 3 routing scenarios (fast low-cost, high-quality, fallback on timeout) * includes one `curl` example and one Python SDK snippet * contains at least 2 assertions that CI can check * lists 3 edge cases and recommended mitigations * links to PRD rollout policy.
Sam (Eng): can the CI run against a lightweight mocked runtime? we shouldn't rely on prod quotas.
Ravi (Docs): yes, we'll add a `--mock-runtime` flag in the example that uses the bundle in `/examples/mocks`. CI will run with mocked deterministic responses.
Jess (Design): UI screenshot will have a callout explaining the fallback toggle, use simple red/yellow/green states. I'll produce a 2-step mock.
Luis (Customer): also add a small FAQ line: "what to expect when fallback is used" and recommended SLAs. customers love that.
Sam (Eng): one more edge case — KV cache cold start causing initial latency spikes. include `warmup` tip and a sample warmup script:
```
# warmup 10 requests
for i in range(10): client.generate(prompt='warmup')
```
Ravi (Docs): perfect. I'll draft the quickstart doc-as-spec and include inline test assertions. Can I get sign-off on acceptance criteria?
Ana (PM): sign-off pending small edits: make the CI assertions less brittle (match substring not full text) and add a short rollback note for Dedicated customers.
Sam (Eng): will relax assertions to `contains` checks. I'll add rollback note.
Ravi (Docs): will push a doc PR with `docs-as-spec` label in 30m. cc @qa-bot for auto-test config.
qa-bot: noted. I'll create an examples test that runs `examples/onboarding-routing/test.sh` against `--mock-runtime` and report pass/fail.
Ana (PM): timeline — doc PR by EOD, engineering review tomorrow morning, design assets by EOD tomorrow. If anyone blocks the PR, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
Luis (Customer): thanks — looking forward to being able to share a copyable example with our team.
Jess (Design): will post drafts in #design later today.
Sam (Eng): will add the `quality_threshold` example + warmup script to the repo branch.
Ravi (Docs): ok, creating PR now. I'll include a short changelog entry for the quickstart.
Ana (PM): awesome — backups: if we hit scope creep, cut the console screenshot and keep the sequence diagram. keep quickstart runnable first.
Sam (Eng): noted.
Ravi (Docs): PR: https://git.redwood/infra/docs/pulls/482 — WIP, comments welcome.
Ana (PM): thanks team, closing thread unless new blockers.
